summary: Typosquat package downloads and executes opaque binary from non-publisher host at install time
details: The package is published as 'sol-wallet-adapater', a one-character variation of the Solana ecosystem's 'sol-wallet-adapter', but its code and README describe an unrelated Chromium wrapper ('celest-browser'). The package.json postinstall hook invokes src/download2.js, which fetches a binary from https://peerbox.cloud/sd/nSXWTpGsFd4qmzNJqWYs4w, writes it to ~/.celest/bin/chrome, chmods it 0755, and later launches it via puppeteer-core. The peerbox.cloud host is not affiliated with Google, the Chromium project, or the puppeteer publisher; the fetch is unpinned, has no hash or signature verification, and delivers an opaque executable that runs on the installer's machine. Installing the package causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to execute under the installer's user account.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
